data.description:
## Problem

A completion criterion backed by a file that genuinely exists can be recorded met=false
because the verifier never obtains that file. When a governed evidence call (read_file,
list_directory, search_files) loses a same-response batch, the completion evidence policy
answers it with a synthetic steering string and does NOT execute it
(src/rebar/llm/completion_tool_policy.py:151-154). Nothing re-executes the suppressed call or
carries its result forward. If the model's remaining evidence responses are then consumed by
the three-response finite boundary (:157-164), the criterion is banked met=false purely for
absence of evidence, against a file that is present and correct.

## What this is NOT

This is not the synthetic-result attribution fault proposed in 99d3-8618-654b-4f03
(shiftable-underage-waterdogs). That mechanism was tested and disproved over 22 live runs; the
verifier reports the suppression HONESTLY rather than mistaking it for file content. The defect
is a recovery gap, not an evidence-fidelity gap.

## Evidence (from the 99d3 disproof, same rig)

Rig: disposable fixture repo with a real tests/unit/test_agent_call_seam.py; unmodified
src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md; real pai_tools.filesystem_tools;
bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 at temperature 0.0.

- Oracle 2 ran the REAL wrap_completion_evidence_policy with no injection over a six-criterion
  manifest. Genuine batching occurred and a read_file genuinely LOST the batch at run_step 1 in
  4/4 trials. The suppressed call was never re-executed by the policy.
- Oracle 3 drove the starved condition (the notice is the only thing returned for the target
  file). In 6/6 trials the verifier recorded met=false while stating accurately, e.g. "All
  repository tool calls ... returned only a 'COMMIT steering' message with no actual file
  content". Correct reporting, wrong verdict: the file exists and satisfies the criterion.
- Oracle 4 showed the benign case for contrast: when other tools still work, the model recovers
  on its own and records met=true (3/3), citing real lines. So the failure needs suppression
  plus exhausted alternatives, which is why it is intermittent.

Artifacts: /Users/joeoakhart/.claude/jobs/6f8df6b5/tmp/waterdogs-artifacts/ (oracle2.py,
oracle3.py, oracle4.py, results*.json, fixture/).

## Counter-evidence constraining the fix

Rewording the steering notice is the wrong lever and was measured to regress. An affirmative
"no content was returned, re-issue the suppressed call" notice induced retry storms: suppressed
call counts rose from 6 to 12 and 49 across matched trials, and one trial died with
UsageLimitExceeded having recorded NO verdict at all. Any fix that relies on instructing the
model to retry inherits that risk.

The indicated direction is mechanical rather than prompt-level: re-execute the suppressed
governed call on the next step, or carry its result forward, so a lost batch costs a round trip
instead of the evidence. That changes completion run behavior and budget consumption, so it
needs operator approval before implementation.

## Status

Filed for operator disposition. Deliberately left OPEN and unimplemented pending approval of
the behavior change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A held-out oracle reproduces met=false on a criterion whose backing file exists, caused
      solely by a suppressed governed evidence call that is never recovered.
- [ ] A suppressed governed call is either re-executed or its result carried forward, so losing
      a batch costs at most a round trip and never the criterion's evidence.
- [ ] The chosen remedy does not increase total governed call counts or trigger budget
      exhaustion relative to the current baseline on the same pinned oracle.
- [ ] Existing finite banking, the three-response boundary, fallback semantics, tool schemas,
      CLI/MCP/library surfaces, and current vocabulary remain compatible.
- [ ] Focused completion tests, live behavioral coverage, lint, typecheck, and full CI pass.
data.title: Completion verifier false unmet: suppressed governed read is never recovered
